hero.headline: Vero Beach group collects donations for Venezuela earthquake relief through Saturday
hero.teaser: Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is hosting a Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive to collect essential supplies for communities devastated by a massive earthquake.
hero.body:
A Vero Beach organization is gathering supplies for communities devastated by a 7.5 magnitude earthquake in Venezuela. Latinas Nexus Network is hosting the Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive, with organizers Lourana Navarro and Juliana Marino, along with Heidi Ramirez, leading the effort. The group is working with Global Empowerment Mission to ensure all donated supplies reach verified humanitarian relief efforts in Venezuela. Navarro, who was born in Venezuela and now lives in Vero Beach, said her family in Caracas is safe but surrounding communities have suffered severe losses. She described the scale of destruction as something that will take decades to recover from, noting that resources are severely limited.

The humanitarian crisis is urgent, with Marino emphasizing that hundreds of thousands of people need immediate assistance. The most critical shortages are food and shelter, along with basic hygiene facilities. Navarro stressed that people currently lack places to sleep and bathe. The organizers are calling on the entire community to contribute, not just the local Hispanic population. "We are asking everyone," the founders said. "They really need us."

The drive accepts a wide range of essential items. Needed supplies include powder Gatorade, non-perishable food, baby formula and baby food, diapers of all sizes, baby wipes, feminine hygiene products, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes and toothpaste, rain boots, toilet paper, blankets, sleeping bags with batteries, flashlights and batteries, heavy duty garbage bags, first aid kits, bandages and gauze, hand sanitizer, cleaning supplies, face masks, nitrile gloves, and plastic bins with lids. Donations can be dropped off at 684 Old Dixie Hwy, Vero Beach, FL 32962.

The collection runs through Saturday, June 27, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. For those who want to contact the organizers directly, Lourana Navarro can be reached at (954) 205-0700, Juliana Marino at (772) 913-0805, or Heidi Ramirez at (772) 213-2747. All donations will be directed through verified humanitarian channels to ensure supplies reach those who need them most.

cards.headline: Missing diver found dead on ocean floor near Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: A missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet Friday afternoon.
cards.body:
The U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding a missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed 4 vessels to assist in the search. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit, which had independently monitored the Mayday call, was already en route to assist. Aerial support was provided by both the Coast Guard and the FWC.

Responding units made contact with the vessel involved nearly due east of Avalon State Park. At approximately 4:10 p.m., civilian divers who were friends of the missing diver entered the water and located him at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. The diver was recovered and pronounced deceased. The deceased was transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce. The body was found approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division is conducting the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, which remains ongoing.

cards.headline: 2 killed in head-on crash on Allapattah Road in Indiantown
cards.teaser: Two people were killed in a head-on crash Saturday morning on Allapattah Road near Martin Highway in Indiantown.
cards.body: Two people were killed in a head-on crash on Allapattah Road, also known as the Allapattah S-Curve, near Martin Highway in Indiantown on Saturday morning. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the crash occurred around 6:30 a.m. at 8113 SW Allapattah Road. Allapattah Road was blocked for approximately 6 hours while the Florida Highway Patrol processed the scene and has since reopened.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds extends commanding lead in Florida governor's race with $66 million war chest
cards.body:
Byron Donalds continues to pull away from his Republican rivals in the race to replace Ron DeSantis as Florida governor. The Naples congressman raised nearly $253,000 for his campaign account and $435,000 for his political committee, Friends of Byron Donalds, during the week ending June 19. With just over 50 days until the primary election, Donalds has accumulated nearly $66 million in available funds. Though a $20 million media buy will reduce his cash on hand in the next reporting period, his financial advantage over the rest of the field remains insurmountable.

The fundraising gap between Donalds and his opponents has grown into a decisive chasm. James Fishback raised only $4,825 to his campaign account and nothing to his Florida First political committee during the same week, leaving him with roughly $117,000 to spend. Notably, Fishback spent more than $60,000 from his committee during the period, including a $5,000 payment to his running mate Sean Lozano. Jay Collins raised just over $11,000 to his campaign account and $1,500 to his political committee, maintaining roughly $3.5 million in available funds. However, nearly $2 million of his committee money went toward an ad buy in the week. Former House Speaker Paul Renner has struggled with fundraising for two consecutive periods, raising less than $30,000 to his campaign account and $13,000 to his political committee. He has roughly $2.5 million to spend.

The weakness across the broader field reflects donor sentiment about the race's direction. The Republican Party of Florida declined to hold a gubernatorial debate at Saturday's Sunshine State Showdown, a decision that drew criticism from trailing candidates seeking opportunities to directly challenge Donalds. Donalds and his allies have argued that a debate is unnecessary given the lack of viable opposition in the race. The latest fundraising reports support this position, demonstrating that donors have not responded to pleas from other candidates to fund a competitive primary.

As Florida Republicans prepare to select their nominee, the contest appears increasingly decided. Donalds' financial dominance combined with his opponents' inability to gain traction with contributors suggests the primary outcome is largely predetermined. Without a debate platform to gain exposure and facing steep funding disadvantages, the trailing candidates appear unable to mount a meaningful challenge to the frontrunner in the remaining weeks of the campaign.

cards.headline: Israel and Lebanon sign framework agreement for peace with U.S. backing, Rubio announces
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio joined Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors in Washington to announce a framework agreement described as a first step toward peace following months of conflict with Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio joined Israel and Lebanon's ambassadors to the U.S. Friday to announce a framework agreement described as a first step toward peace following months of conflict between Israel and the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah. The agreement was signed in Washington by Yechiel Leiter, the Israeli ambassador to the United States, and Nada Hamadeh Moawad, the Lebanese ambassador to the United States. The agreement does not include Hezbollah and prompted one of the group's officials in Lebanon to warn of civil war.

The State Department said the framework establishes a process for dismantling Hezbollah and for Lebanon to regain territory taken by Israeli forces. The U.S. will facilitate a newly created Military Coordination Group for Lebanon to implement the framework while committing $100 million in humanitarian assistance. The State Department stated the framework provides "a genuine pathway out of a long crisis" for Lebanon and "creates a verifiable path to removing the persistent threat on its northern border" for Israel. Leiter said achieving peace depends on Hezbollah being disarmed and dismantled, which will allow Israel to withdraw and Lebanon to regain its full sovereignty. Moawad said the framework is "a first step on the road to restoring Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity, securing a permanent and final cessation of hostilities, enabling our people to go back to their land."

cards.teaser: Two people were killed in a head-on crash on Allapattah Road near Martin Highway in Indiantown Saturday morning.
cards.body: Two people were killed in a head-on crash along Allapattah Road near Martin Highway in Indiantown on Saturday morning. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, the crash occurred around 6:30 a.m. at 8113 SW Allapattah Road, along a stretch known as the Allapattah S-Curve. The Florida Highway Patrol processed the scene while Allapattah Road remained closed for about six hours. The road has since reopened. The identities of the two people killed have not been released.

cards.headline: West Boca Raton homeowner battles repeated delays for My Safe Florida Home grant after completing work
cards.teaser: Anne Bendel of West Boca Raton completed storm hardening work on her home and paid $8,000 out of pocket, but her My Safe Florida Home grant remains in limbo aft.
cards.body:
Anne Bendel of West Boca Raton completed storm hardening work on her home and paid $8,000 out of pocket, but her My Safe Florida Home grant remains uncertain after repeated requests for additional documentation. Bendel first contacted WPTV in May when her grant was held up by paperwork from her insurance company. That issue was resolved, and representatives with My Safe Florida Home told her status was complete in May. A week later, representatives asked for more documentation, including a permit of completion for a large impact window. After Bendel provided it, questions arose about dates, and her application is now back under review.

Bendel said she does not have a computer and is handling the entire process on her phone without help, describing the experience as gut-wrenching. The My Safe Florida Home program has helped thousands of homeowners across the state with grants of up to $10,000 to fortify homes against storms and earn insurance discounts. Bendel said she completed all required work, obtained necessary permits, and secured the insurance they requested. She said it seems like when everything is done, they find some other task to send, because they know when she had the work done. WPTV has contacted the Florida Department of Financial Services in Tallahassee about Bendel's case and the status of her grant.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce's Florida Highwaymen Museum Featured in America 250 Road Trip Celebrating Nation's Birthday
hero.teaser: A museum that opened this year in Fort Pierce is part of the festivities celebrating the country's 250th birthday.
hero.body:
A museum that opened this year in Fort Pierce is part of the festivities celebrating the country's 250th birthday. The city announced on its Facebook page this week that the Florida Highwaymen Museum is a featured stop on the America 250 Road Trip.

The museum celebrates 26 Black artists who began painting in the 1950s, creating bold, colorful landscapes of Florida's untouched beauty and selling them along the roadside when segregation kept them out of traditional galleries. Located at 1234 Avenue D, the museum is the nation's only one with exhibitions that include paintings from each of the 26 renowned Highwaymen artists.

The museum operates summer hours from June 16 through July 31 on Saturday and Sunday from noon to 4 p.m. The museum will be closed in August and reopen in September, featuring a new exhibit.

Fall and spring hours of operation from Sept. 1 through June 15 will be expanded. The museum's summer schedule runs through the end of July before the temporary closure.

cards.headline: West Boca Raton Homeowner Battles My Safe Florida Home Grant Delays Despite Completed Work
cards.teaser: Anne Bendel says her efforts to receive a promised grant from the state to fix up her home keep facing one hurdle after another, even though the work is complete and she has paid $8,000 out of pocket.
cards.body:
Anne Bendel, a West Boca Raton homeowner, says her efforts to receive a My Safe Florida Home grant have faced repeated obstacles despite completing all required work. She first contacted WPTV in May regarding her grant being held up by paperwork from her insurance company, an issue that was eventually resolved. "My Safe Florida Home contacted me, set me to a task and said my status was complete in May," Bendel said. However, a week later, representatives asked for additional documentation: a permit of completion for a large impact window. After she provided it, questions arose about dates, and her application was sent back under review.

Bendel said she has completed the work, obtained permits, and secured the insurance the program required, yet her hopes for grant money toward the $8,000 she paid out of pocket remain uncertain. "I did the work, I had it completed, I got the permits, I had the insurance they asked for. Everything is done, but it seems like when everything is done they find some other little task to send you," Bendel said. She expressed that the process has shaken her confidence in the program's promises. WPTV has contacted the Florida Department of Financial Services in Tallahassee regarding Bendel's case and the status of her grant.

cards.headline: Alligator Alcatraz Detainees Scattered Across U.S. After Everglades Facility Closes
cards.teaser: With the controversial detention facility now closed, detainees have been moved to facilities in Louisiana, Texas, New Mexico and as far as Tacoma, Washington, creating challenges for families and immigration attorneys.
cards.body:
With the closure of the controversial Alligator Alcatraz detention facility in the Florida Everglades, immigration officials have transferred detainees who were not deported to facilities across the country. According to immigration attorney Richard Hujber, those held at the facility have been sent to Louisiana, Texas, New Mexico, and as far away as Tacoma, Washington. "I had a client moved all the way to Tacoma, Washington, like it can't get farther than that," Hujber said. The geographic dispersal of detainees poses serious legal challenges for those seeking bond hearings and to remain in the United States. Hujber explained that different federal circuit courts apply different standards when considering bond requests. "There's different laws in different circuit courts in different parts of the country," he said, noting that some circuits have ruled against bond approval more frequently than others. This inconsistency means that a detainee might qualify for release in one jurisdiction but face denial in another.

For many immigrants, the inability to secure bond forces difficult decisions about whether to continue fighting for residency or asylum or to accept self-deportation. Gov. Ron DeSantis reported that roughly 21,000 people were deported from the facility since it opened nearly a year ago. For some families, the closure brought relief. Anna Maria Hernandez's cousin was detained at Alligator Alcatraz and was released just before closure, now under an order of supervision that allows him to drive, work, and live in the U.S. The Baker County facility in North Florida remains operational, but for many former detainees and their families, uncertainty about the future persists.

hero.headline: SoFlo Market brings Independence Day celebration to Boca Raton City Hall on July 4
hero.teaser: The free monthly market will feature a kids parade, DJ, vendors, gourmet food, face painting, mini golf, and balloon twisting at Boca Raton City Hall.
hero.body:
The SoFlo Market will turn Boca Raton City Hall into a hub of Independence Day celebration Saturday, July 4, from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m., founder and organizer Tatiana Freitas said. The free event at 201 West Palmetto Park Road will feature a kids parade, a DJ, unique vendors, gourmet food, and the first 20 children through the gate will receive a free gift. Family entertainment includes face painting, a foggy bubble station, mini golf, and balloon twisting, alongside handmade crafts and desserts.

Boca Raton firefighters and police officers have been invited to share the day with residents. Kyle, Freitas' son, and Eddie, her husband, are part of the organizing team ensuring activities run smoothly. Electricity will be powered by generators on-site. A live appearance by the SoFlo Market's flamboyant flamingo mascot is set to be a crowd favorite.

Freitas told WPTV the market's mission is to uplift small local businesses and bring the community together. The SoFlo Market runs monthly, but Freitas said the Independence Day edition is always a standout. The event's Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube channels will feature behind-the-scenes clips and photos throughout the day.

cards.headline: Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League urges pet owners to prepare hurricane disaster plans
cards.teaser: The rescue league recommends microchipping pets, creating emergency kits with three days of supplies, and identifying pet-friendly shelters before the next storm.
cards.body:
With hurricane season in full swing, Peggy Adams Animal Rescue League is urging South Florida residents to create a disaster plan for their pets before the next storm hits. Dr. Alyssa Comroe, CEO of Peggy Adams, told WPTV the safest place for pets during a hurricane is right alongside their owners. The shelter's expert team recommends ensuring pets wear a collar with current identification and have an updated microchip registered with correct contact information.

Pet owners should prepare an emergency kit containing a three-day supply of food and water in airtight containers, bowls, a sturdy carrier, bedding, towels, medications for two weeks, vaccination records, first-aid supplies, litter and box for cats, leashes, harnesses, cool packs, wipes, waste bags, and multiple forms of visible ID. The rescue league also recommends introducing pets to a designated safe room ahead of time, such as a walk-in closet or downstairs bathroom, and conducting practice runs so the hurricane isn't their first time there. Pet owners should keep a printed list of local pet-friendly shelters and hotels in an accessible place and maintain recent photos of pets, ideally with their owner, to help with identification if separated. Florida's hurricane season runs June through November.

cards.headline: George Snow Scholarship Fund in Boca Raton awards record $7.5 million to 470 students
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton nonprofit has now distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties.
cards.body:
The George Snow Scholarship Fund, headquartered in Boca Raton, awarded more than $7.5 million in scholarships and support services to 470 students across Palm Beach and Broward counties in 2026, President Tim Snow told WPTV. Founded over 40 years ago, the nonprofit has distributed more than $45 million to over 4,100 students, making it the largest scholarship provider in Palm Beach County. The program is designed to bridge the gap between traditional financial aid and what students and families can afford, offering four-year commitments to ensure stability throughout college.

Vice President of Development Jay Brandt noted that the fund's services extend beyond financial assistance, providing mentorship, professional development, and resources like the College Compass podcast. One 2026 recipient, Zya Chow, a Wellington Community High School graduate planning to attend Georgetown University, earned both the Royal Palm Hearing Aid Scholarship and the Davidowitz Family Caregiving Youth Scholarship. The Doyle-Whelchel Scholars Boutique, led by Scholar Services Coordinator Garvey Antoine, offers professional, formal, and casual wear to help scholars prepare for interviews, internships, and campus life. The boutique accepts donations of new or gently used clothing, footwear, and accessories.

cards.headline: Florida Mango Festival showcases 75 vendors, rare varieties at West Palm Beach Convention Center
cards.body:
The Florida Mango Festival will feature more than 75 vendors at the Palm Beach County Convention Center on Saturday, June 27, showcasing local mango varieties, grafted trees, tropical fruits, and mango-themed products. Festival co-organizer Vince Rogers highlighted some of Florida's most distinctive mango cultivars, including Fruit Cocktail, which features a sweet multi-layered flavor profile, Orange Sherbet with creamy citrus notes, and Pineapple Pleasure offering tropical pineapple undertones. Rogers noted that Florida produces more than 350 mango varieties, far exceeding what consumers typically encounter in grocery stores. "Our backyard-grown Tommy Atkins are just much, much more superior to anything you're going to find at a store," Rogers said.

Alex Salazar of Tropical Acres Farms explained that the air-conditioned indoor venue provides an ideal setting for visitors to taste, learn, and discover Florida-grown mangoes while avoiding summer heat. Throughout the day, Salazar will lead educational demonstrations on home mango growing and grafting techniques, offering tips for both beginners and experienced growers. The festival will also feature an "ID Your Mango" booth, a scion exchange for online mango community members, and a display of Florida's diverse mango cultivars. General admission begins at 10:30 a.m., with early entry at 9 a.m. for first pick ticket holders. The convention center is located at 650 Okeechobee Boulevard in West Palm Beach. Tickets are available at floridamangofestival.com.

cards.headline: Collins and Renner challenge Donalds at Florida GOP confab after debate cancellation
cards.teaser: Denied a formal debate at the Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown, Lt. Jay Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner used their speaking slots to directly criticize front-runner Byron Donalds.
cards.body:
The Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown did not include a gubernatorial debate despite the lopsided race. Lt. Jay Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner voiced their criticisms of front-runner Byron Donalds, a Congressman from Naples, in a room where Donalds was present. Second Lady Layla Collins delivered extended remarks before her husband's speech, emphasizing the importance of moral compass and fighting for what is right rather than pursuing headlines or social media attention. Collins directly challenged Donalds' viability, comparing him to Charlie Crist and warning that Florida Democrats chair Nikki Fried would attack Donalds' vulnerabilities in a general election. Collins predicted Democrats would question Donalds' character, his exploding net worth after going to Washington, stock trades, drug dealing connections, crime, and money and influence relationships, scrutinizing every headline, disclosure, and transaction.

Renner largely avoided personal attacks while outlining his military service, prosecutorial background, and tenure as House Speaker as evidence he would deliver results as governor. He emphasized the importance of electing someone ready to handle unexpected challenges, referencing the 2018 election uncertainty between Ron DeSantis and Andrew Gillum. Renner claimed he was the only candidate who fought against special interests and woke school board members, spending over $2 million on school board races and opposing Amendment 3 and 4. Before Donalds' question-and-answer segment, Sen. Rick Scott reiterated his endorsement, calling Donalds Florida's next Governor.

cards.headline: DeSantis praises World Cup visitors while Florida politics faces backlash over divisive rhetoric
cards.teaser: Ron DeSantis praised the World Cup for giving visiting fans a chance to see America directly, but critics note his own political brand is built on rhetoric painting a grim picture of internal threats.
cards.body:
Ron DeSantis praised the World Cup for giving visiting fans from other countries a chance to see America directly. "We do have a really great country," DeSantis said. "I know there's a lot of problems. I know we see a lot of things that we wish we could change immediately. And I know there's a lot of work to do, but I wouldn't want to be anywhere else." He noted that visitors have gotten to see firsthand both the generosity of the American people and that this is a good country. However, DeSantis' own political brand is built substantially on the premise that a vast, organized internal enemy is destroying the country. Teachers and school administrators who discussed gender identity in classrooms were called groomers. Corporate executives who supported diversity programs were described as carriers of the woke mind virus. California was described as a civilization in decay leading an attack on the American family.

Trump has made similar arguments in far more extreme terms. On Veterans Day 2023, at a campaign rally in New Hampshire, he declared: "We pledge to you that we will root out the communists, Marxists, fascists and the radical left thugs that live like vermin within the confines of our country." A month later, he described immigrants arriving in the United States as poisoning the blood of the country. The World Cup has produced what American political culture cannot seem to produce on purpose: a setting in which people from wildly different countries interact with actual Americans and discover that the caricature is wrong. Fans from Scotland, Iran, Brazil, Morocco, and Australia arrived with whatever impressions their politics and media had given them and found something different.

cards.headline: Largo mayor reads Pride Month proclamation after residents object to plan to drop it
cards.teaser: Largo Mayor Woody Brown opened the June 2 Commission meeting by reading a Pride Month proclamation after the city had planned to drop it from the agenda entirely before dozens of residents showed up to object.
cards.body:
Largo Mayor Woody Brown read a Pride Month proclamation at the June 2 Commission meeting after the city had initially planned to remove it from the agenda. Dozens of residents objected to the planned omission and attended the meeting, many arriving directly from the ribbon-cutting for Horizon West Bay, an $85 million mixed-use development anchored by the city's new City Hall. The same Commission recently passed an ordinance creating the Sip and Stroll entertainment district in downtown blocks surrounding City Hall, which allows patrons to carry drinks purchased from approved local businesses through designated zones. Abner Morales, owner of Wepaa Puerto Rican Restaurant nearby, is designing custom branded cups for the program.

Brown faced real pressure over the proclamation decision, as new state legislation barring local governments from spending on diversity, equity and inclusion-related events takes effect in January. During a June 1 online chat with residents, Brown explained that with the city budget unsigned, the Governor could potentially cut off funding streams Largo depends on, including dollars for stormwater infrastructure. Commissioner Michael Smith, who is gay, pushed back against the near-removal of the proclamation, describing it as a slap in the face and recounting 28 years spent in the closet and past suicidal thoughts tied to his identity.

cards.headline: Florida gubernatorial candidate pays running mate $5,000 as campaign funds dwindle
cards.teaser: James Fishback raised $4,825 to his campaign account and nothing to his political committee in the week ending June 19, while spending more than $60,000 including a $5,000 payment to running mate Sean Lozano.
cards.body:
James Fishback raised $4,825 to his campaign account and nothing to his Florida First political committee in the week ending June 19. He had roughly $117,000 total to spend as of that date. He spent more than $60,000 from the committee alone during the week, including a $5,000 payment to running mate Sean Lozano that pushed the would-be lieutenant governor's haul past $25,000. Fishback may be the only candidate paying someone to be on the ticket in the Republican gubernatorial primary.

The other candidates face their own cash troubles as they struggle to compete with Byron Donalds, who added nearly $253,000 to his campaign account and $435,000 to his Friends of Byron Donalds political committee during the same week, bringing his total to nearly $66 million on hand. Jay Collins raised a little more than $11,000 to his campaign account and $1,500 to his political committee, with roughly $3.5 million to spend. Former House Speaker Paul Renner raised less than $30,000 to his campaign account for the second consecutive period and $13,000 to his political committee, with roughly $2.5 million to spend. No candidates will debate at Saturday's GOP Sunshine State Showdown event.

cards.headline: Long shot Florida gubernatorial candidate Bobby Williams cites divine call to run
cards.teaser: Bobby Williams avoided controversy at the Republican Party of Florida event with an autobiographical speech that discussed his journey in Christ and how God lobbied him to run for Governor over a period of years.
cards.body:
At the Republican Party of Florida's Sunshine State Showdown, the gubernatorial primary field took the stage without a traditional debate format despite complaints from candidates trailing front-runner Byron Donalds. Lt. Jay Collins and former House Speaker Paul Renner seized the opportunity to level criticism at the Congressman from Naples, who participated in a question-and-answer session instead. Collins' wife, Second Lady Layla Collins, delivered extended remarks characterizing her husband as having the moral compass needed to win a general election. Collins himself directly challenged Donalds' viability, warning that Florida Democrats and party chair Nikki Fried would attack Donalds' record in Congress, his net worth increase, stock trades, and financial disclosures during a potential general election matchup.

Renner avoided personal attacks and instead highlighted his background in the military, as a prosecutor, and as Speaker as evidence he could deliver results as governor. He emphasized readiness to handle unexpected crises and claimed to be the only candidate in the race willing to fight special interests. Bobby Williams, another long shot candidate, took a different approach with an autobiographical speech centered on his Christian faith and his conviction that God called him to run for governor. Sen. Rick Scott reiterated his endorsement of Donalds, declaring him Florida's next governor.

cards.headline: Missing diver found dead on ocean floor 6 miles off Fort Pierce Inlet
cards.teaser: A missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet on Friday afternoon, according to the St.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is investigating after a missing diver was found dead on the ocean floor approximately 6 to 7 miles north-northeast of the Fort Pierce Inlet. The U.S. Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce received a Mayday call over VHF Channel 16 at approximately 11:30 a.m. Friday regarding the missing diver. Following the distress call, the Coast Guard notified the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, which immediately deployed 4 vessels to assist in the search. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit had independently monitored the Mayday call and was already en route to assist.

A group of civilian boaters who were friends of the missing diver departed the Fort Pierce Inlet at approximately 1 p.m., with aerial support provided by both the Coast Guard and FWC. Responding units made contact with the vessel involved nearly due east of Avalon State Park. At approximately 4:10 p.m., civilian divers entered the water and located the missing diver at the bottom of the ocean in approximately 55 feet of water. The diver was recovered and pronounced deceased. The deceased was transported to Coast Guard Station Fort Pierce, and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Criminal Investigations Division is conducting an ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident.

cards.headline: Vero Beach group collecting earthquake relief supplies for Venezuela through Saturday
cards.teaser: Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is hosting a Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive to collect essential supplies for communities devastated by a massive earthqu.
cards.body:
Latinas Nexus Network in Vero Beach is hosting a Venezuela Earthquake Relief Drive to collect essential supplies for communities devastated by a 7.5 magnitude earthquake in Venezuela. The drive is being organized by founders Lourana Navarro and Juliana Marino, along with Heidi Ramirez. Donations can be dropped off at 684 Old Dixie Hwy, Vero Beach, through Saturday, June 27, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The organizers are working with Global Empowerment Mission to ship the collected supplies to Venezuela, and say 100 percent of donated supplies will be directed through verified humanitarian relief efforts.

Navarro, who was born in Venezuela and now lives in Vero Beach, said her family in Caracas is safe, but surrounding communities have lost everything. She said the scale of destruction will take years to address. Marino said hundreds of thousands of people are in need right now, with the worst needs being food and places to sleep and bathe. The drive is open to everyone, not just the local Hispanic community. Organizers are collecting powder Gatorade, non-perishable food, baby formula and food, diapers, baby wipes, feminine hygiene products, soap, shampoo, toothbrushes and toothpaste, rain boots, toilet paper, blankets, sleeping bags with batteries, flashlights and batteries, garbage bags, first aid kits, bandages and gauze, hand sanitizer, cleaning supplies, face masks, nitrile gloves, and plastic bins with lids. To contact organizers, call Lourana Navarro at (954) 205-0700, Juliana Marino at (772) 913-0805, or Heidi Ramirez at (772) 213-2747.
